title: Boeing Keeps Sliding: Why Citi Sees 56% Upside
detail:

C

Boeing Keeps Sliding: Why Citi Sees 56% Upside ©pixelshot via Canva
Key Takeaways

Boeing stock is down 28% in six months. It fell nearly 11% on Tuesday after third-quarter results pushed its $10 billion free cash flow target out to 2029.

On Oct. 28, Citi kept its Buy rating and $260 target, 56% above the current price, while many other firms cut their targets.

Analysts now expect Boeing to earn $3.48 a share in 2027, down from $6.46 a year ago.

Buying for Citi's $260 means paying today for cash Boeing doesn't expect until 2029, and January's 2027 delivery plan is the next test.

Boeing (BA:NYSE) stock is down 28% in six months, including a drop of nearly 11% on Tuesday after its third-quarter report. On Wednesday, Citi analyst John Godyn kept his Buy rating and $260 target, 56% above the current price.

The $10 billion just moved to 2029

CEO Kelly Ortberg warned in September that getting 737 production steady at 47 a month was taking longer than expected. On the third-quarter call he said "it will take us into next year to get fully stable at this rate."

In Tuesday's report, Commercial Airplanes lost $697 million in the third quarter.

The bigger hit was Boeing's new cash plan: about $2 billion of free cash flow this year, $3 billion in 2027, $6 billion in 2028 and $10 billion in 2029. Before the report, analysts had penciled in $5.5 billion for 2027 and $9.8 billion for 2028.

Citi isn't budging

Citi has had its $260 target since May. This week at least 11 other firms cut their targets. That leaves Citi's 4% above the $249 consensus.

The bull case is in the release: a record $745 billion backlog and FAA certification of the 737-7 and 737-10. Ortberg said "the range of outcomes is narrowing."

TIKR tracks 28 analysts on Boeing. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Boeing, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Boeing's Analyst Ratings

Does $260 add up?

Wall Street's average target has barely moved in a year, even as the stock fell [25%]:

The Boeing (BA): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

This week's cuts pulled it to $249 on Wednesday, from $265 the day before.

The earnings behind those targets have moved a lot more. Analysts expect a loss this year, then $3.48 a share in 2027 and $6.92 in 2028:

The Boeing (BA): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

That 2027 estimate was $6.46 at the end of September 2025, and it's still falling.

With a loss expected this year, Boeing's 112x forward P/E tells you little, and so does the 173x that Citi's target implies. From 2014 to 2019, Boeing's forward P/E averaged 18.8x. Getting to $260 at anything close to that takes earnings analysts don't expect until around 2030.

When rotation reaches extremes: Here are Citi’s preferences

Investing.com -- Citi told clients in a new note that European equities have experienced one of the sharpest rotations on record, with defensive stocks outperforming cyclicals by a margin usually seen only during major market stress.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Strategist Beata Manthey noted that over the past three weeks, defensives have gained 9% while cyclicals have fallen 4%. Rallies in healthcare and staples outpaced sell-offs in tech, banks and basic resources.

He added that the relative performance of cyclicals versus defensives, adjusted for the broader STOXX 600, has breached a -3 standard deviation threshold. That level was matched only in 2008, 2020 and 2022.

Unlike those episodes, the European index remains near its highs. Citi said this suggests a rotation-driven event rather than outright capitulation.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The bank said the rotation could ease or reverse in the near term as risk sentiment improves. However, history shows that such extreme rotations are typically followed by several months of choppy leadership rather than a sustained cyclical rebound.

Manthey added that European cyclicals still trade at a sizable valuation premium to defensives, despite a slowing earnings outlook and stretched positioning.

"As a result, we remain cautious on chasing a full-blown Cyclical recovery too early," she wrote.

Citi continues to favor a barbell approach.

"We continue to favor a barbell approach; Healthcare is our preferred Defensive, which we pair with select Cyclical exposure via Tech, Banks, and Basic Resources," the strategist said.

title: Citi Says the NAND Shortage Will Last Until 2028. Here’s Why Sandisk Stock Is Still So Cheap.
detail:
Citi Says the NAND Shortage Will Last Until 2028. Here’s Why Sandisk Stock Is Still So Cheap.
Jabran Kundi
Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:09 AM EDT 5 min read
SNDK
C
MU
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

On October 1, Citi reaffirmed its Buy rating on SanDisk (SNDK) following Micron's (MU) results showing a 42% quarter-over-quarter increase in NAND revenue and roughly 30% higher prices. Citi forecasts that the NAND industry will remain supply-constrained through 2028. SanDisk's own results already reveal how quickly market conditions have shifted.

Contracts Built to Outlast the Cycle

SanDisk reported a 372% year-over-year revenue increase to $8.97 billion last quarter, with higher prices contributing two-thirds of the sequential growth. Data center now represents 38% of its bits, compared with 12% a year earlier, reflecting growing AI demand for flash storage.

The risk is that price-led growth can reverse with the cycle. Citi noted that Micron's supply growth is higher than SanDisk's mid-teens industry expectation, and it forecasts industry bit shipments growing in the mid-20% range in 2027 and 2028. What stands out is the company's response. It is responding by locking in demand through 10 multi-year agreements with eight customers. These deals are worth at least $93.9 billion at floor pricing and are supported by $16.5 billion in financial guarantees. Together, they cover more than half of fiscal 2027 bits and approximately two-thirds of fiscal 2028 bits. The floors protect less than current earnings.

A 6.9x Multiple Prices In a Downturn

SanDisk trades at a forward P/E of just 6.9x, roughly 68% below the sector median of 21.72x. This discount likely reflects fears that current memory earnings are close to their cyclical peak. Analysts forecast a 203% jump in EPS this fiscal year, followed by slower growth of 23.96% in fiscal 2028 and a 3.58% decline in fiscal 2029. Investors are typically reluctant to pay a premium for earnings they believe are near a cyclical peak.

In my view, the stock looks undervalued if its contracts remain intact. The CFO expects attractive margins even at floor pricing, with contract margins around 80%. The company also has $4.76 billion in cash, almost no debt, and a $15.5 billion buyback authorization.

If its contracts protect margins, I believe SanDisk is trading below a reasonable valuation for a five-year investment.

title: Are Options Traders Betting on a Big Move in Citigroup Stock?
detail:
Are Options Traders Betting on a Big Move in Citigroup Stock?
Zacks Equity Research
Thu, October 29, 2026 at 7:56 AM EDT 2 min read
C
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investors in Citigroup Inc. C need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the Dec. 18, 2026 $30 Call had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

What is Implied Volatility?

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

What do the Analysts Think?

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for Citigroup shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, Citigroup is a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) in the Financial - Investment Bank industry that ranks in the Top 23% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 30 days, three analysts have increased their earnings estimates for the current quarter, while two have dropped their estimates. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter from $2.40 per share to $2.39 in that period.

Given the way analysts feel about Citigroup right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there's a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

The fair value estimate for AMC Entertainment Holdings has shifted from US$3.12 per share to US$3.37 per share, pointing to a modestly higher central valuation in current models. Analysts linking this change to recent commentary describe a mix of cautious optimism, with higher price targets sitting alongside ongoing concerns about leverage and long term box office pressures. What Wall Street Has Been Saying
🐂 Bullish Takeaways

B. Riley raised its AMC Entertainment price target to US$3.25 from US$2.50 after updating estimates ahead of Q3 earnings for theater stocks. This points to slightly improved expectations within its valuation range, even as the rating remains Neutral.

Citi lifted its AMC Entertainment price target to US$2.20 from US$1.80 after the company reported quarter to date revenue of US$1.33b, which the firm notes sits above consensus and reflects higher attendance.

🐻 Bearish Takeaways

Citi continues to rate AMC Entertainment as Sell and highlights concerns about the company's leverage, which it views as a key risk factor for equity holders.

Citi also points to what it calls secular headwinds facing the box office, which it sees as a constraint on the company's longer term growth prospects even with better recent revenue figures.

The refinancing simplifies AMC Entertainment's capital structure, reduces stated interest expenses and cost of capital, and eases near term liquidity pressure, although the company still carries high leverage with ongoing liquidity and dilution risks.

AMC Entertainment reported worldwide box office attendance at its locations up 13.5% in the second quarter and highlighted premium screens and expanded group events as support for operating performance.

title: Citi's Andy Sieg Still Recommends Private Credit Despite Market Volatility
detail:
Citi's Andy Sieg Still Recommends Private Credit Despite Market Volatility
Darryn Pollock
Wed, October 28, 2026 at 6:53 PM EDT 2 min read
C
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Photo by BeInCrypto

Andy Sieg, who heads Citi's wealth management unit, said the bank still recommends private credit to clients. Withdrawal requests at non-traded private credit funds are running well above their typical 5% quarterly caps.

Those funds, known as business development companies (BDCs), hold multiyear loans but allow periodic withdrawals. Some clients therefore cannot cash out in full.

Does Citi's Private Credit Confidence Match Market Pricing?

Sieg made the case on CNBC's Halftime Report, calling private credit and private equity long-term building blocks rather than trades.

He said clients invest for 10 to 30 years, so the test is whether a diligence team vets each manager.

"clients have been happy with the returns that they've had"

Andy Sieg, head of Citi Wealth, on CNBC

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zwkg2J_sJtI

Meanwhile, many listed BDCs trade 10% to 20% below the reported value of their holdings, Valuation Research data showed.

The same preliminary data show requests at 11 of the 14 largest non-traded BDCs averaged 13.0% in the third quarter. That was down from 13.9% in the second. However, it remains well above the typical 5% limit.

In an October blog, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) flagged private credit as a possible amplifier of market stress. It said borrowers could draw on committed direct-lending credit lines if conditions tighten, straining fund liquidity.

How Much of Citi's Wealth Growth Is Organic?

Wealth revenue has grown for 10 straight quarters. The third-quarter gain was 15% from a year earlier.

A record $38 billion in fresh client money, which Citi calls net new investment assets, flowed in during the quarter. Existing clients supplied most of it by shifting more holdings to the bank, according to Sieg's memo.

Net interest income rose 20% while noninterest revenue grew 5%, Family Wealth Report data showed. Deposit income therefore drove more of the gain than investment fees.

Still, Sieg said organic flow growth, which excludes market gains, topped 10%, despite acknowledging market tailwinds.

How clients respond to capped withdrawals could show whether private markets stay core holdings across wealth platforms.
